symptoms: Light and dark green mottling (mosaic pattern) on young leaves
Leaves may be narrow, fern-like, or stringy
Stunted uneven growth, poor fruit set, brown streaks inside fruit possible
No fungal growth, no rot: pattern and stunting are the clues

severity_cues.early: Mosaic mottling on a few plants
severity_cues.advanced: Widespread stunting and fern-leaf growth, fruit quality loss

favorable_conditions: Spread by hands, tools and infected seed or debris; Tobacco users carry it on fingers; it survives in soil and crop residue

treatment.summary: No chemical cures a plant virus. Contain it: remove infected plants, disinfect everything, use clean seed
steps: Uproot and destroy symptomatic plants, handle them last in the round
Disinfect tools and stakes with 10 percent skim milk or trisodium phosphate solution
Do not smoke or chew tobacco in the field, wash hands with soap before working
For the next season: use certified virus-free or resistant seed, and rotate
Control weeds and volunteer tomato plants nearby, they host the virus
organic: 10 percent skim milk spray as a mechanical virus suppressant on hands and tools
Certified disease-free seed, two-year rotation, residue destruction

source.org: TNAU Agritech Portal, crop protection, tomato diseases
source.title: Tomato: viral disease management

safety_notes: No spray is involved: the safety comes from sanitation discipline
Infected plants must be destroyed, never composted
